current_date: Updated December 2025 (typo correction to HIA requirements made February 2026)
current_evidence: The council's validation download page (downloads/download/136, linked from 'Download the latest guidance' on the planning validation page) offers only this Appendix 1 file and the Appendix 2 checklist; the document text says 'Updated December 2025' and notes a February 2026 correction.

issues.detail: Planning Statement is the only Householder requirement Grokbot lists, but the source explicitly excludes householder applications. The local Householder checklist items Grokbot missed are archaeological assessment, ecological survey and mitigation report, flood risk and drainage assessment, landscaping details and tree survey (all conditional). The FRA section also names residential extensions under 250 sqm in Flood Zones 2/3 or a critical drainage area.
issues.evidence: Section 26: 'required for all Major and Non-Major planning applications (except those for trees and householder applications)'; Appendix 2 Checklist 5 (Householder) lists archaeology, ecology, flood risk & drainage, landscaping, tree survey as 'Yes / No'.

issues.detail: Listed building consent is marked '(none)', but the source requires a Heritage Statement for all Listed Building Consent applications. Appendix 2 Checklist 3 also lists marketing information, structural survey, archaeology, landscaping, nutrient neutrality, planning statement, sustainability statement and tree survey as conditional items for LBC and conservation area consent.
issues.evidence: Section 16 Heritage Statement: 'Listed Building Consent applications;' and Appendix 2 Checklist 3 (Listed Building Consent / Conservation Area Consent).

issues.detail: Outline, Reserved matters, Advertisement consent and Demolition in conservation area are all marked '(none)', but the source has checklists for them. Checklist 2 (Outline & Reserved Matters) applies the same conditional local list as Full applications, and the Feb 2026 correction concerns HIA for Reserved Matters. Checklist 4 (Advertisement) lists heritage statement, lighting impact assessment and planning statement. Conservation area demolition triggers a heritage statement, structural survey and marketing information.
issues.evidence: Appendix 2 Checklists 2, 3 and 4; Section 28 Structural Survey covers 'demolition or structural impacts in conservation areas'; Section 21 Marketing covers demolition of buildings in conservation areas.

issues.detail: Grokbot places Landscaping scheme and Structural Survey under 'Change of use - prior approval'. The source applies Landscaping to planning applications EXCEPT changes of use. It applies Structural Survey to planning applications for conversion of rural buildings and conservation-area or listed-building demolition, not to prior approvals. Landscaping is also missing from the Full and Householder rows where it does apply.
issues.evidence: Section 18: 'Planning applications (except those for the change of use or alteration to an existing building), where landscaping would be a significant consideration'.

issues.detail: About 38 requirements are tagged 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning'. Examples are Air Quality, Archaeology, Heritage Statement, Schedule of works (listed building) and Telecommunications statement. The source's Appendix 2 checklists name the application types for each item, so the guesses were unnecessary. Some are wrong: the listed building schedule of works and telecom mast statements are not general Full planning items.
issues.evidence: Appendix 2 has separate checklists for Full, Outline/RM, LBC/CAC, Advertisement and Householder.

issues.detail: BNG, Design and Access Statement and Fire Statement all reuse the same contents-page fragment as their trigger, so none states when the item applies. The source's Fire Statement trigger is buildings with 2+ dwellings or educational accommodation that are 18m+ or 7+ storeys.
issues.evidence: Grokbot: 'Design and Access Statement (where required) Biodiversity Net Gain (see section 12) Fire Statements (see section 13) Local Requirements 7.'; Source s13: 'Contain two or more dwelling or educational accommodation; and Meet the height condition of 18m or more in height, or 7 or more storeys.'

issues.detail: Several triggers are copied from the wrong section. Noise uses kitchen extraction text; the source trigger is noise-sensitive development or uses causing disturbance. Ventilation/Extraction uses sustainability text ('natural ventilation... green infrastructure'). Waste/Refuse storage uses a transport servicing-plan bullet. Planning Obligations uses self-build principal-residence text; the source trigger is a pre-application indication that a S106 is needed. 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal' reuses the Agricultural Land Classification trigger.
issues.evidence: Source s22 Noise: 'applications that raise issues of disturbance, or are considered to be noise sensitive developments'; s25: 'where the local authority have indicated at pre-application stage that a Section 106 agreement would be necessary'.

issues.detail: 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' has the trigger 'a robust sequential test', which comes from the Town Centre Use (retail) section, not flood risk. The Retail/Town Centre row gives only the edge-of-centre under-250 sqm case. It misses the main triggers: sequential test for main town centre uses outside designated centres (300 sqm+ in local centres), and impact assessment for retail, leisure or office of 200 sqm+ outside the Town Centre or local centres (over 300 sqm in local centres).
issues.evidence: Section 31: 'retail, leisure and office development with a floor area of 200m² or above, not located in the Town Centre or a local centre'.

issues.detail: Some triggers are only contact details. Air Quality gives a phone number and a purpose statement; the source triggers are a 5%+ traffic increase within an AQMA, or biomass boilers or CHP plant.
issues.evidence: Grokbot: 'please contact the Local Planning Authority or HBC Environmental Protection on 01429 284024'; Source s9: 'Where a development would lead to a minimum 5% increase in traffic within an Air Quality Management Area (AQMA)'.

issues.detail: Several triggers are fragments or say the opposite of the source. Archaeology: 'a development, Desk Based Assessment ... 1.'; the source says it applies to applications that may affect a heritage asset or its setting. Environmental Statement: 'of an Environmental Impact Assessment is not necessary.' LVIA: 'a full LVIA as part of an EIA is not necessary' (inverted); the source says it is needed where location is a significant consideration. Flood Risk: 'a simple flood risk assessment is required.' has no location or size condition. Ecology is cut off at 'unless an exception applies: 23'. Heritage Statement: 'also include a Heritage Statement (see requirement 15)' (Heritage is s16). Nutrient Neutrality has only the calculator sentence and leaves out the in-scope uses: new dwellings, student accommodation, care homes and tourist accommodation.
issues.evidence: Source s11: 'Planning applications that may affect the significance of any heritage asset, including its setting'; s14: 'Development within a local authority's own identified critical drainage area, Flood Zones 2 & 3'; s23: 'New dwellings, student accommodation, care homes, tourism attractions and tourist accommodation'.

issues.detail: 'Employment / Economic Statement' is listed as a Full planning requirement, but the quoted text says it is optional and not needed for validation. 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' is encouragement, not a validation requirement.
issues.evidence: 'Applicants can also submit an Economic Statement ... if they so wish but this would not be required for validation purposes.'

issues.detail: Several tab_items are boilerplate or contact text: the GDPR paragraph with phone number 01429 266522, 'Personal Information will be handled ... Appendix 1- National and Local Validation Requirement Notes...', the email submission instruction (developmentcontrol@hartlepool.gov.uk), and 'Information on parking and servicing can be combined within the Transport Assessment...'.
issues.evidence: Tab 'Submission rules' items 1-3; 'Drawing / document standards' item 4.

issues.detail: Several tab_items are heading fragments with page numbers or are cut off before the list they introduce. Examples: 'Nitrate Pollution of the Teesmouth & Cleveland Coast SPA/Ramsar site 24.', 'Nitrate Pollution ... When is this required?' (a duplicate heading), 'This includes housing developments which have an indirect 28 impact...', 'A Nutrient Neutrality assessment is required for the following types of in scope applications:' (no list follows), and '...must be provided at A1 ... 16 9.'
issues.evidence: Tab 'Policy-driven requirements (all application types)' and 'Submission rules'.

issues.detail: The Residential Visual Amenity Assessment is not captured. The source says it may be needed for solar farms, onshore wind and other large-scale developments, decided case by case, alongside the Local Landscape Visual Assessment (s20).
issues.evidence: Section 20: Residential Visual Amenity Assessment for 'developments such as solar farms, on shore wind proposals and other large scale developments'.

issues.detail: List date 2025-12-01 matches 'Updated December 2025'. However, the document also records a February 2026 typo correction to the HIA requirements for Reserved Matters, and the file and download titles still say 'August 2025', which may confuse users.
issues.evidence: Section 2.1: 'A correction to a typo was made in February 2026 in respect to the aforementioned HIA requirements'.

summary: Grokbot's link is the current Hartlepool local list, and the December 2025 date is right (a February 2026 correction is also noted). The extraction is weak: many triggers are fragments or come from the wrong section, Householder is given the one requirement the source excludes for householders, and LBC, Outline/RM, Advertisement and conservation-area demolition are wrongly shown as having no local requirements despite the source's Appendix 2 checklists.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
